literal: Able to be firm and to be yielding—then weight may be borne;
idiomatic: Be firm when you must and yielding when you may, and heavy burdens will still be borne.

literal: Able to be trusting and to be compliant—then danger may be passed;
idiomatic: Be steadfast in trust and supple in compliance, and even perilous paths may be walked.

literal: Able to be wise and to be foolish—then one's span may be long.
idiomatic: Know when to show wisdom and when to feign ignorance, and your days may endure.

literal: The men of the Zhou ancestral temple thrice sealed their mouths.
idiomatic: Men of the Zhou ancestral temple sealed their lips three times over.

literal: The leaky cup set before; the tilting vessel kept behind.
idiomatic: Keep the leaky cup before your eyes and the tilting vessel at your back.

literal: May all who come after receive it and pass it at the right hand.
idiomatic: May posterity take it up and keep it at the right hand.

literal: Afterward many ministers said the Wei History was untrue; Wucheng again ordered a further review, and Shou revised it once more.
idiomatic: Later many officials declared the Book of Wei unreliable; Emperor Wucheng ordered another review, and Shou revised it again.

literal: Thereupon he wrote a biography for Lu Tong; Cui Chuo was moved back out and appended separately.
idiomatic: He then composed a biography for Lu Tong and moved Cui Chuo's entry back out as a separate appendix.

literal: In the Yang Yin family biography it had read, "Since Wei there has been only one house in the clan"—now he changed these eight characters;
idiomatic: In the Yang Yin family biography the text had read, "Since Wei there has been only one house in the clan"—he now altered those eight characters;

literal: and where it had first said "a man of Hongnong, Huayin," he changed it to "claims to be of Hongnong," to match Wang Huilong's claim to be a man of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: and where it had first said "of Hongnong, Huayin," he changed it to "claims Hongnong," to match Wang Huilong's claim to be from Taiyuan.

literal: These were his errors.
idiomatic: These were his lapses.

literal: Before long he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Secretariat Supervisor.
idiomatic: Before long he was appointed director of the palace secretariat and concurrently secretariat supervisor.

literal: When Wucheng died, mourning had not yet been proclaimed.
idiomatic: When Wucheng died, mourning had not yet been publicly announced.

literal: The ministers within the palace, because the Later Sovereign had already reigned for years, were uncertain about an amnesty edict.
idiomatic: The inner ministers, since the Later Sovereign had already reigned for years, doubted whether an amnesty should be issued.

literal: The ministers brought Shou in for consultation; Shou firmly held that favor ought to be shown, and they followed him.
idiomatic: They summoned Shou for counsel; Shou insisted that grace was due, and they followed his view.

literal: He directed edicts and rescripts, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and in general supervised the Five Rites, with rank as Special Advance.
idiomatic: He directed edicts and rescripts, was made right vice director of the masters of writing, and oversaw the Five Rites in general, with the rank of special advance.

literal: Shou memorialized asking Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to join him in supervision.
idiomatic: Shou memorialized asking Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to serve as co-supervisors.

literal: He first told Shikai; Shikai, startled, declined on the ground that he was no scholar.
idiomatic: He told Shikai first; Shikai, alarmed, declined on the ground that he was no scholar.

literal: Shou said: "All affairs under Heaven are decided by Your Highness; the Five Rites cannot be settled without Your Highness.
idiomatic: Shou said, "All affairs under Heaven are yours to decide; the Five Rites cannot be settled without you.

literal: " Shikai thanked him and agreed.
idiomatic: " Shikai thanked him and consented.

literal: He brought in many men of letters to take up the brush; the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui in fact directed the work.
idiomatic: He brought in many literary men to draft the text; the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui actually directed the work.

literal: In the third year of Wuping he died.
idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he died.

literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with posthumous title Wenzhen.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works and left vice director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

literal: His collected works ran to seventy scrolls.
idiomatic: His collected works ran to seventy scrolls.

literal: Shou was a great scholar of vast talent, yet by nature narrow-minded and unable to accept fate and embody the Way.
idiomatic: Shou was a great scholar of vast talent, yet by nature narrow and unable to accept fate or embody the Way.

literal: When he met the powerful and noble of the day, he would always please them with a pleasant countenance.
idiomatic: Before the powerful and noble of his day he always wore a pleasing countenance.

literal: Yet he lifted up the younger generation and put reputation and conduct first; men flashy, frivolous, and rash—though they had ability, he did not esteem them.
idiomatic: Yet he championed younger men and put character before talent; flashy, frivolous, and reckless men he would not honor, however able they were.

literal: At first Xing Zicai of Hejian and his brother Jijing were famed for letters together with Shou; the age called them Great Xing and Little Wei, saying Wei was the sharper.
idiomatic: Early on Xing Zicai of Hejian and his brother Jijing had won fame for letters alongside Shou; the age called them Great Xing and Little Wei, saying Wei was the keener wit.

literal: Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai would often say, "The Buddha helps the great man of the lodge.
idiomatic: Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai would often say, "The Buddha aids the lodge's towering man."

literal: " Later Shou gradually vied with Zicai for renown; Wenyuan belittled Zicai, saying, "Your talent does not match Wei Shou's.
idiomatic: Later Shou began to rival Zicai for renown; Wenyuan slighted Zicai, saying, "Your talent cannot match Wei Shou's."

literal: " Shou grew all the more elated.
idiomatic: Shou grew all the more triumphant.

literal: In his autobiography he wrote: "At first they spoke of Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei.
idiomatic: In his autobiography he wrote, "At first they named Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei."

literal: " Yet inwardly Shou looked down on Xing and would not concede it in his heart.
idiomatic: Yet inwardly he despised Xing and would not admit it.

literal: Once Shou fell ill, he loved music and was skilled at barbarian dance.
idiomatic: When Shou fell ill he took to music and was skilled at barbarian dance.

literal: At the end of Wenyuan's reign he several times on the Eastern Hill staged monkey-and-dog fights with performers; the emperor doted on him familiarly.
idiomatic: At the end of Wenyuan's reign he several times on the Eastern Hill staged monkey-and-dog fights with performers; the emperor treated him with familiar affection.

literal: His mother's sister's son Cui Yan of Boling once mocked him with shuang-sheng wordplay, saying: "Fool-Wei, fade-Shou.
idiomatic: His mother's sister's son Cui Yan of Boling once mocked him with paired-alliteration verse, saying, "Fool-Wei, fade-Shou."

literal: " Shou replied: "Yan-face, rank-lean—whose whelp are you? Sheep-jaw, dog-cheek; knob-head, flat-nose. Meal-barracks, tuckah-cage—stop-hole, sting-mock.
idiomatic: Shou replied, "Yan-face, rank-lean—whose whelp are you? Sheep-jaw, dog-cheek; knob-head, flat-nose. Meal-barracks, tuckah-cage—stop-hole, sting-mock!"

literal: " His nimble retort was unrestrained in just this way.
idiomatic: His repartee was as nimble and unrestrained as that.

literal: Once he held the brush of history, he earned much resentment from others.
idiomatic: Once he held the historian's brush, he earned much resentment.

literal: In the year Qi fell, Shou's tomb was opened and his bones cast out.
idiomatic: In the year Qi fell, Shou's tomb was opened and his bones thrown out.

literal: He had earlier adopted his nephew Renbiao as heir; Renbiao rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Board of Provisions.
idiomatic: He had earlier adopted his nephew Renbiao as heir; Renbiao rose to gentleman of the masters of writing in the board of provisions.

literal: In the Sui Kaihuang era he died in office as magistrate of Wen county.
idiomatic: In the Sui Kaihuang era he died in office as magistrate of Wen county.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
